updates.rationale:
Samsara is at $41.36, about 3% below the $42.70 stop, and a sale has been waiting for your approval since October 16 — 16 proposals and counting. I want to be direct about that: the price line the last thesis drew has been crossed, and the case for approving the sale is real. What's changed since the last refresh is that the Q3 print is now expected around November 26, roughly ten days away, and the stock is sitting on its rising 50-day average ($40.95) in what the chart calls a base. The business remains solid — ARR at $2.125 billion growing 30% for three straight quarters, four consecutive GAAP profitable quarters, and guidance raised twice in a row. But Q3 guidance pointed to 24% revenue growth, down from 30%, and that deceleration is what the market is pricing in. No insider buying, no estimate revisions in four weeks, and a stock down 17% year-to-date don't give me a reason to override the stop with fresh conviction. I'm keeping the thesis LONG and the stop where it is; the sale proposal already waiting for you is the right answer unless the Q3 report changes the picture.

[The plan's levels stay as they were set. This refresh's own: stop $42.7.]
